title: Synchronous Remote Database Metadata Lookups at Admission Control/Deploy Time
pattern: An admission controller or deployment enforcement point performs synchronous, blocking network queries to an external, centralized database to verify artifact metadata or provenance based on a hash key.
why_bad: The lookup creates a tight dependency on the availability of the external database at deploy time. If the database fails, the deployment system must fail-open (reducing security) or fail-closed (halting system recovery). It also dramatically increases validation latency, often exceeding SLOs.
detection: An admission webhook or deployment validator issuing synchronous RPC or database network calls inside its verification loop.
counterexample: Checking local file systems or caching layers with sensible fallback logic. Marked as `Contextual`.
source: Google SRE, *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (2020), Chapter 14, "Ensure Unambiguous Provenance", p. 115-117.
